title: State renaming preserves guarded runs
statement: Let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $\Gamma$ be an alphabet, and let $k$ be the number of work tapes. Suppose $M_{\mathrm{src}}$ and $M_{\mathrm{host}}$ are nondeterministic machines over $\Gamma$, with state sets $S$ and $H$, respectively, and let $e:S\hookrightarrow H$ be an embedding and $G\subseteq S$. Assume that for every choice bit, every $q\in G$, and every input and work-tape reading, the host transition at $e(q)$ is the source transition at $q$ with its successor state renamed by $e$. For a source configuration $c$ on input $x$ and a choice word $w$, suppose every state reached from $c$ under each prefix of $w$ of length strictly less than $|w|$ belongs to $G$ whenever the run has a state; then the host run from the state-renamed configuration $e(c)$ under $w$ equals the source run from $c$ under $w$ with its state renamed by $e$.
